# Results — Study 898 (Managed-Vol Equity)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Moreira & Muir (2017), *"Volatility-Managed Portfolios"*: scale equity **inversely to
recent volatility** and the Sharpe ratio rises. Rebuilt honestly on daily SPY vs bills:
`weight = min(2.0, 0.12 / RV_21d)` of SPY, the rest in BIL, daily rebalance, **exactly one
execution lag** (the weight for day *t* uses only returns through the close of day *t−1*).
Every race is **excess-of-cash on both legs** (SPY − BIL vs managed − BIL). Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
The sample is pinned as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped and the sample never creeps). Fingerprint `f7ef586be44c` (SPY+BIL
closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **SPY** (equity leg) and **BIL** (the 1–3-month T-bill ETF, the **real cash leg** — not an assumed 0%) |
| Window | 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 (**4,802** aligned closes, ~19 years, ann = **252**); BIL's live history starts 2007-05-30, so the excess-of-cash sample begins there |
| Rule | `w_t = min(2.0, 0.12 / RV(21d)_{t−1})` of SPY, `1 − w_t` in BIL; daily rebalance; grid over targets {10/12/15%} × windows {21/42/63d} |
| Execution | **one lag**: the trailing-vol estimate through close *t−1* sets the weight earning day *t*'s return (`shift(1)`) |
| Cash / rf | the un-invested fraction earns the **BIL total return**; the levered fraction max(w−1, 0) pays a retail borrow spread over bills. Every Sharpe race is **excess-of-cash on both legs**, so the cash yield cancels |
| Costs | one-way bps × \|Δw\| × NAV per daily rebalance (entry trade excluded, both legs pay it); borrow on the levered fraction. Sweep 1 / 2+0.5% / 5+1% |
| Survivorship | single-asset study — SPY is the surviving US-equity benchmark, BIL the surviving bill ETF; no cross-sectional panel bias, but the ~19-year single tape is a **short-history** caveat, named on the Signal axis |

## Headline race — 12% target, 21d window, cap 2.0×, gross, excess-of-cash

| leg | excess-CAGR | ann vol | **Sharpe** | max DD | terminal wealth |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **managed-vol** | +8.26% | **13.4%** | **0.659** | **−31.1%** | ×4.51 |
| buy & hold SPY | +9.35% | 19.9% | 0.549 | −56.5% | ×5.45 |

Sample 4,780 days; average weight **0.96** (nearly fully invested on average), levered
(w > 1) **41.5%** of days (at the 2.0× cap 3.5%); turnover **9.15× NAV/yr**.

- **HAC alpha** (Moreira-Muir regression, managed-excess on B&H-excess): **+2.78%/yr**,
  Newey-West *t* = **+1.67**, β = 0.56, appraisal 0.36 — positive, **below the *t* ≥ 2 bar**.
- **Sharpe advantage**: **+0.110** (0.659 vs 0.549), but the paired block-bootstrap 95% CI
  is **[−0.128, +0.355]** and **straddles zero** (Pr[gap < 0] = 0.195).

## Is it "just" leverage-timing? The decomposition

A *constant* scale leaves the Sharpe ratio unchanged, so **the entire Sharpe gap is the
timing** — the question is whether that timing is a genuine risk-adjusted pickup. Split the
managed mean excess return `mean(managed) = β·mean(B&H) [exposure] + α [timing]`:

| component | value |
|---|--:|
| exposure (β · mean B&H) | +2.407 bps/day |
| timing (α) | +1.102 bps/day |
| net managed − B&H daily mean | **−0.822 bps/day** (HAC *t* = −0.97) |

Because β = 0.56 < 1 the managed book gives up **raw** excess return (−0.82 bps/day, a
−1.09 pp/yr excess-CAGR give-up); the **+1.10 bps/day timing alpha** buys the smoother,
lower-vol path that lifts the Sharpe — but that alpha is *not* statistically certified
(*t* = +1.67). With average weight 0.96 the drawdown cut is genuine **de-risking in the
storms**, not merely holding less.

## The thermostat — does it deliver the promised constant vol? (the mechanical half — yes)

Rolling-21d realized vol of the **managed** excess return: median **12.5%** (target 12%),
p10–p90 **8.8%–17.4%**, inside a ±5-pt band **86.0%** of days. Buy & hold: median 13.4%,
p90 **27.8%**. The thermostat works — it clips the vol spikes SPY leaves wide open.

## The heart-attack ledger — max drawdown (excess-of-cash NAV) per crash window

| window | managed-vol | buy & hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| GFC 2008-09 | **−30.6%** | −56.5% |
| 2018 Q4 | −18.0% | −19.8% |
| COVID 2020 | **−13.7%** | −33.9% |
| 2022 bear | **−15.2%** | −25.0% |
| **full sample** | **−31.1%** | **−56.5%** |

And the shield is **timing, not just holding less**: against 200 shuffled-vol placebos (same
weight distribution, no alignment with tomorrow's risk) the placebo mean max DD is **−57.4%**
and **0/200** shuffles reach a drawdown as shallow as the observed −31.1% — **p = 0.000**.
That clears the desk bar on the real tape.

Two robust patterns: the **Sharpe gap is positive in all nine cells** (+0.085…+0.117) and

## Robustness — two eras (split 2016-01-01)

| era | alpha | *t* | Sharpe (BH) | max DD (BH) |
|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| 2007-05 → 2016-01 (n=2,143) | +2.18% | +0.96 | 0.449 (0.347) | −31.1% (−56.5%) |
| 2016-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,637) | +2.59% | +1.08 | 0.827 (0.759) | −18.0% (−33.9%) |

The Sharpe gain and the drawdown cut hold in **both** halves — not one era's artefact — but
the alpha *t* is weak in each (0.96 / 1.08): the sign is stable, the significance is not.

## Costs & whipsaw — the overlay is cheap to run

Turnover 9.15× NAV/yr; one-way bps × \|Δw\| daily + retail borrow on the levered fraction.

| one-way cost + borrow | Sharpe | gap | alpha (HAC *t*) | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bp | 0.652 | +0.103 | +2.69%/yr (+1.62) | −31.2% |
| 2 bp + 0.5% borrow | 0.639 | +0.090 | +2.51%/yr (+1.52) | −31.2% |
| 5 bp + 1.0% borrow | 0.613 | +0.063 | +2.16%/yr (+1.30) | −31.4% |

Costs never flip anything — the drawdown shield and the Sharpe gap both survive 5 bp + 1%
borrow essentially intact (the book is only mildly levered, so borrow rarely bites). But
what fails the bar gross (**alpha *t* = 1.67**) also fails it net.

## Placebo — shuffled vol signal, 200 seeds (same exposure, no timing)

| quantity | observed | placebo (200 shuffles) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| HAC alpha | **+2.78%/yr** (*t* = +1.67) | mean −0.11%/yr (sd 2.03) | **0.070** |
| Sharpe gap | **+0.110** | mean −0.055 | **0.050** |
| max drawdown | **−31.1%** | mean −57.4% | **0.000** |

The two halves split cleanly: the **drawdown shield is unambiguous timing** (p = 0.000 — no
same-distribution random weight reproduces it), while the **alpha / Sharpe gain is only
borderline** (p = 0.070 / 0.050 — roughly one shuffle in fifteen does as well).

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful (30 seeds, 6,000 days)

| world | mean alpha *t* | share *t* ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|
| NULL — risk priced (μ_t ∝ σ_t²) | **−0.01** (sd 1.32) | 7% |
| PLANTED — leverage effect (mean falls as variance rises) | **+4.98** (α ≈ +9.4%/yr) | 97% |

With risk fully priced the overlay earns nothing (mean *t* centred on zero); with a planted
vol-return disconnect it lights up on nearly every seed. The harness can bank the effect when
it exists — so the real-tape *t* = 1.67 is a property of the **tape**, not of the machinery.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED (Real on the tail control · Weak on the Sharpe).** The
  drawdown-taming half is **real on the real tape**: full-sample max DD **−31.1% vs −56.5%**
  (COVID −13.7% vs −33.9%), robust across all nine grid cells and both eras, and certified as
  genuine *timing* by the shuffled-signal placebo (**p = 0.000**, 200 seeds) — with average
  weight 0.96 it is de-risking-in-storms, not just holding less. The **Sharpe/return half is
  not certified**: the +0.110 Sharpe gain has a bootstrap CI straddling zero
  ([−0.128, +0.355]), HAC alpha **+2.78%/yr at *t* = 1.67** (never above 2 on the grid, era
  *t* = 0.96 / 1.08, placebo p = 0.070). Single ~19-year tape — short-history, named.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Mechanically ideal: turnover 9.15× NAV/yr (~1 bp costs ~9
  bps/yr), SPY capacity is effectively unlimited, any brokerage can run it, and every number
  survives 5 bp + 1% borrow. But what survives certification is **risk control, not excess
  return** — you deploy it knowing you *gave up* ~1.1 pp/yr of excess CAGR (β = 0.56 < 1) for
  a smoother, shallower-drawdown path, and the Sharpe uplift that would make it an *edge*
  never clears *t* = 2. A real shield, not a certified paycheck — FRAGILE, not INVESTABLE.
